rationale: Both responses decompose the brief the same way: revenue forecasting or segmentation, deal scoring, budget-gap alerting, stage prediction and loss-reason NLP, over a similar data model and pipeline. A has strengths of its own. It ranks deals by expected value (probability times amount times strategic weight), adds a survival model for time-to-transition, SHAP explanations and a refresh cadence. Its code snippets are illustrative but loose: it predicts on the training data and implies k-means clusters map neatly onto BCG quadrants. B is slightly stronger on soundness and actionability. It defines concrete evaluation criteria per model (MAPE, AUC with top-20% revenue capture, macro-F1, cluster validation with AEs) and gives forecast bands. It maps each model directly onto the business decisions the user asked about, in a decisions table. It also lays out a phased rollout ending in an A/B test of AE adoption, which closes the loop on whether the system actually raises revenue. B has a flaw too: it uses loss-reason embeddings as a feature for scoring open deals, a leakage risk. On balance B's evaluation and decision framing tip it.
